question.problem: Approximate the value of $\sqrt{37}$ using the tangent line approximation of $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$ at $x=36.$
question.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $x=a$ is

$$
L(x)=f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

In our case, we have $a=36,$ which gives

$$
L(x)=f(36)+{f}^{′}(36)(x-36).
$$

Let's compute $f(36)$ and ${f}^{′}(36)$ in the expression above. Evaluating the function, we get

$$
f(36)=\sqrt{36}=6,
$$

and computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt{x})=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}},\end{aligned}
$$

which in turn gives

$$
{f}^{′}(36)=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{36}}=\frac{1}{12}.
$$

So, the tangent line approximation is

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x)=6+\frac{1}{12}(x-36).\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $\sqrt{37}$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=37.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{37} & ≈L(37) \\  & =6+\frac{1}{12}(37-36) \\  & =6+\frac{1}{12} \\  & =\frac{73}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$
